name: Sunken Basin
geological_features: A continent-sized impact basin depressed three kilometers below the surrounding highlands
Dense atmosphere pooling in the basin creating a pressure differential
Volcanic hotsprings along the basin floor
Eroded rim mountains surrounding the depression
specific_features: Ruins of prefabricated structures half-consumed by jungle growth
description: Sunken Basin is defined by an ancient impact crater so vast it constitutes its own biome. The basin floor sits well below the planetary mean elevation, and the dense atmosphere pools within it like an invisible sea, creating significantly higher pressure and temperature than the surrounding highlands. Jungle vegetation chokes the basin floor in impenetrable tangles.

Within the basin, the air is hot, wet, and oppressively heavy. Sounds carry with unnatural clarity, and visibility is reduced by perpetual haze rising from geothermal vents. The highlands above the rim offer cooler, thinner air and sweeping views of the green cauldron below.

The ruins found on the basin floor suggest a previous colonization attempt, likely dating to the early expansion era. Records of the settlement have been lost, and the structures show signs of rapid abandonment rather than gradual decay. What drove the colonists away remains unknown, as the planet appears hospitable despite its challenging climate.

Sunken Basin's geothermal resources and rich botanical biosphere make it attractive for renewed settlement. The failed colony, however, gives prospectors pause. Several survey teams have reported an inexplicable sense of unease within the basin, though environmental scans reveal nothing harmful. The jungle keeps its secrets well.
